You embed with an enterprise team, find the work that actually warrants AI, architect the system, build it, and stay long enough to make it survive contact with production. This is a three-way role: consultant, operator, engineer. You should be as comfortable pressure-testing a business case with a COO or VP of Engineering as you are diagnosing why retrieval quality collapsed after a data refresh. The people who succeed here can hold a discovery conversation on Monday and ship what they scoped on Thursday. On this track, your edge is data, retrieval, and model behavior: you make agents trustworthy by getting the data, context, and evaluation right. We work with regulated industries and Fortune 500 clients who have AI mandates, real constraints, and low tolerance for demos that don’t hold up. How We Approach The Work FDEs are trusted to shape the solution, not only deliver it. Every engagement calls for architect-level judgment: Reframes the request. Treats “we need an agent for X” as a hypothesis, not a spec. Decomposes the problem. Outcome → process → decisions → data → systems → actors → constraints — before choosing technology. Chooses the intervention. Remove, simplify, traditional software, automation, LLM, RAG, agent, or multi-agent — and defends why. Owns the architecture decision. Documents trade-offs (ADRs), sets success metrics, pushes back on scope that won’t deliver value. Consultative Discovery Clients rarely arrive with a fully formed problem, and the FDE’s first contribution is helping them see it clearly. You lead discovery with genuine curiosity, moving the conversation from stated requirements to underlying needs, and you build credibility through the depth of your understanding rather than the breadth of your pitch. Uncovers business drivers. What outcome matters, what it’s worth, why now, and what happens if nothing changes. Uncovers personal drivers. What each stakeholder is measured on, what they’re worried about, and what a win looks like for them individually. Surfaces constraints early. Security, compliance, data access, budget, skills, politics, timelines — the things that kill projects in month two. Aligns stakeholders. Spots conflicting goals between business, engineering, and risk, and brings them to a shared definition of success. Asks strategic questions. Follows the answer with “why,” “how do you know,” and “what happens today when…” — without interrogating. Clients leave the conversation understanding their own problem better. Earns authority through depth. Credibility comes from the quality of the questions and the insight in the playback, not from pitching technology. What You'll Do Discover. Run workshops and process discovery with business, data, and engineering stakeholders. Assess data readiness honestly. Separate genuine AI problems from workflow problems wearing an AI costume. Structure the process and the spec. For any business process being automated, map the current state, decision points, data inputs, and exceptions, then turn it into specifications that both people and AI systems can execute against reliably. Architect & design. Design agentic systems end to end with emphasis on context and retrieval architecture — data sourcing, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, permissions-aware retrieval, knowledge graphs where warranted — plus orchestration, MCP/tool integration, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Build. Ship working systems — agents, retrieval services, evaluation tooling, and the data flows that feed them. Prototypes that prove value in weeks, not slideware. Engineer the delivery system. Own CI/CD for what you build, extended to AI: prompt and context versioning, eval suites that run in the pipeline and gate releases. Operate (Day 2). Own what happens after launch — eval harnesses, groundedness and retrieval metrics, observability and tracing, cost and latency management, drift, and the handoff that lets the client’s team run it without you. Consult. Present to and defend decisions in front of CTOs, VPs of Engineering, CDOs, and business leadership. Quantify impact in their terms. Support pre-sales scoping and proposal work when the deal calls for it. Advanced English is required. Successful completion of a four-year college degree is required. Hands-on experience with frontier AI developer tools including Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or OpenAI Codex. Track record of leading client-facing discovery calls, asking "why" before "how" to decompose unstructured business problems. Solid understanding of architecture paradigms such as RESTful APIs, microservices, and event-driven systems. Well-versed in agentic orchestration tools and frameworks like LangGraph, LangChain, N8N, or direct Model Context Protocol (MCP) and LLM APIs. Skilled at exercising end-to-end delivery ownership and managing project scope without requiring product manager supervision. Ability to work through new and difficult issues and contribute to libraries as needed. Ability to create and maintain continuous integration and delivery of applications. Forensic attention to detail. A positive mindset and a can-do attitude. Experience working on Agile / Scrum teams. Meaningful experience working on large, complex systems. titulo: Senior Business Analyst - Latin America, Remote
descripcion: Bluelight is a leading software consultancy dedicated to designing and developing innovative technology that enhances users' lives. With a steadfast commitment to delivering exceptional service to our clients, Bluelight excels in its focus on quality and customer satisfaction. Our mission is not only to create cutting-edge applications but also to foster a collaborative and enriching work environment where each team member can grow and thrive. With a presence across the United States and Central/South America, Bluelight is in an exciting phase of expansion, continually seeking exceptional talent to join its dynamic and diverse community. We're looking for a Business Analyst to turn business problems into clear, buildable requirements. You'll sit between our clients, our product team, and our engineers: running discovery, mapping processes, writing user stories and acceptance criteria, and making sure what we ship actually solves the problem it was meant to solve. You'll work across a mix of client builds, client maintenance engagements, and Bluelight's internal products, and you'll play a key role when new projects are being scoped and estimated. Responsibilities Lead stakeholder interviews and workshops with clients and internal teams to understand goals, current workflows, and pain points. Document current-state and future-state processes, business rules, data definitions, and edge cases. Support new-project sizing by breaking scope into epics and stories that engineering can estimate with confidence. Identify assumptions, risks, dependencies, and open questions early, and drive them to resolution. Write clear user stories with testable acceptance criteria in Jira. Partner with the Product Manager to prioritize and groom the backlog ahead of each two-week sprint. Work with UI/UX design in Figma to make sure flows and screens match the requirements, and flag gaps before development starts. Answer engineering questions during the sprint and keep requirements current as decisions are made. Work with QA to make sure acceptance criteria translate into solid test coverage. Support sprint demos and coordinate user acceptance testing with clients. Keep requirements documentation organized in Google Drive so decisions and their rationale are easy to find later. Make sure compliance, security, and audit requirements (including SOC 2 considerations) are captured as explicit requirements, not afterthoughts. Act as a trusted point of contact for clients on scope and requirements questions. Translate between business and technical audiences clearly and without jargon in either direction. Surface scope changes early and help the team and client understand the tradeoffs. Requirements 3+ years as a Business Analyst, Product Analyst, or similar role on software projects. Strong experience writing user stories and acceptance criteria in an agile/Scrum environment. Proven ability to run discovery sessions and turn ambiguous input into structured requirements. Comfort with process mapping and data modeling at a business level (flows, entities, relationships, rules). Hands-on experience with Jira; familiarity with Figma and collaborative docs. Excellent written and spoken English; comfortable leading client meetings with U.S. stakeholders. Enough technical literacy to have productive conversations with engineers about APIs, integrations, databases, and system constraints. Nice to Have Experience in an agency, consultancy, or software services environment juggling multiple clients. Exposure to regulated or compliance-heavy domains (e.g., SOC 2, telecom/outbound compliance, education, fintech). Experience writing requirements for integrations with third-party platforms. Familiarity with web application stacks (e.g., Laravel, React) and AWS. Experience supporting estimation or proposal work for new projects. Company Benefits Competitive salary and bonuses, including performance-based salary increases. Generous paid-time-off policy Flexible working hours Work remotely Continuing education, training, conferences Company-sponsored coursework, exams, and certifications Being a consultant in our team is a fun, challenging, and rewarding career choice. Your contributions are highly valued by clients, and the work you do often has a direct and significant impact on their business. You will have the opportunity to work on a variety of projects for our incredible clients, which will accelerate your career growth. You’ll collaborate with modern technologies and work alongside some of the best professionals in the industry! If you’re eager to be part of an exciting, challenging, and rapidly growing consultancy, we encourage you to apply. Show more Show less

Engineer AI-driven test lifecycle management systems that extract scenarios from documentation, utilize self-healing mechanisms, and optimize Playwright performance. Construct automated anomaly detection pipelines that link performance shifts and user issues across monitoring tools, delivering actionable root-cause intelligence. Develop rigorous evaluation frameworks for AI processes, auditing metrics such as precision, latency, and operational expenditure to ensure output reliability. Treat prompt design and context engineering as core technical disciplines, ensuring they are version-controlled and thoroughly validated like traditional codebase components. Modernize test data orchestration, automating the creation and masking of high-fidelity datasets for non-production environments. Drive quality intelligence reporting initiatives, replacing static documentation with interactive dashboards highlighting ROI and automation efficacy. Partner with Backend, DevOps, QA, and Product teams to identify and automate high-friction or repetitive activities across the software development lifecycle. Deploy AI capabilities while adhering to regulatory and security standards like ISO 27001, maintaining the strict confidentiality of credentials and production assets. Ensure dedicated focus on AI architecture and tooling by balancing proactive system development (80%) with targeted support for existing manual QA efforts (20%). Develop systems that effectively hand off complex anomalies to the Human QA team, ensuring AI empowers the critical peer-review lifecycle. Qualifications A minimum of 3 years of professional experience in software, automation, or platform engineering. Advanced proficiency in Python for architecting robust tools and services rather than basic scripting. Expertise in LLM API implementation, including advanced prompt engineering, RAG, tool calling, and agentic workflows. Deep understanding of API orchestration and designing automated systems that interact with live infrastructure. Hands-on experience managing CI/CD pipelines, specifically utilizing GitHub Actions. Command of SQL for direct data validation and database integrity checks. Familiarity with Playwright or similar E2E frameworks, with the ability to optimize suite stability. The ability to evaluate non-deterministic AI outputs through rigorous engineering and validation frameworks. Knowledge of LLM-specific security vectors, including prompt injection mitigation and automated data sanitization. Preferred Skills Knowledge of JavaScript or TypeScript. Analyst IT – Oracle EBS (Finance) is a technical expert in finance modules such as Account Receivables (AR), Account Payables (AP), General Ledger (GL), FA (Fixed Assets), Sub Ledger Accounting (SLA) and PA (Projects) specifically on Oracle E-Business Suite of applications with strong technical skills, implementation, and process related experience in Oracle EBS Modules. You will be working on multiple projects in Oracle R12 version with focus in the domain of EBS Finance modules. This position also works on cross-functional modules in the environment of Quote to Order (Q2O) or Order-to-Cash (O2C) and Procure-to-Pay (P2P) cycles with possible integration of third-party systems. Essential Duties And Responsibilities Production support (Technical and Functional) of Oracle R12 Finance and other related modules. Provides technical support to resolve Finance related issues. Submits and follow up on service requests to Oracle. Supports the development activities for process improvement initiatives. Provides programming of custom code and migrates the solutions to production. Participates in testing/validation activities. Creates Technical and Functional documentations related to any development activities. Examples include BR100 and technical design documents for custom objects. Provide analysis, problem resolution and improvement plan for finance applications. Conduct gap-analysis and work with business team and functional architects to enhance AP, AR, GL, PA, SLA, and FA modules. Support the implementation of solutions through a formal process including requirements gathering and definition, gap analysis, design, development, configuration, project planning, testing and deployment. Provides techno-functional expertise in all Oracle Finance related applications. Manage and support L1 & L2 production along with code migration of fixes and enhancements. Manages the techno-functional documentation related to Oracle Finance Applications. Ensures that the documentation is up to date. Requirements And Preferred Skills 5-7 years of experience Graduate in Business, Finance or Computer Science. Master’s degree is desirable. At least 6 years of direct experience with Oracle EBS R12 Financial module viz., (AP, AR, GL, FA, PA and iProcurement) Candidate should have at least 2 full life cycle implementation experience with hands-on configuration, implementation and support using Oracle EBS in a manufacturing environment. Strong technical expertise in Oracle EBS modules including AP, AR, GL, FA, with cross-functional knowledge of OM and Inventory. Solid understanding of Oracle Applications including Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, EBTax, Purchasing, General Ledger, Fixed Assets, Inventory, and Order Management. Experience with inbound interfaces such as AP Invoice, AR Invoice, and GL Interface. Knowledge of Oracle APEX and Java is an advantage. Expertise in Oracle Workflow and/or OAF, with strong verbal, written, documentation, and training skills. Extensive experience with Oracle Forms, Reports, Workflow, SQL*Loader, Oracle APIs, PL/SQL, database concepts, Unix Shell Scripting, and Oracle Database upgrades. Strong report development skills using Oracle Report Builder, Discoverer, and XML Publisher. Proven ability to collaborate with Planning, Commercial, Finance, and IT teams. Strong understanding of Oracle schema, integration points, data conversions, and technology processes. Advanced development experience with PL/SQL, Triggers, Procedures, APIs, Interfaces, and RICE components. Experience with Oracle implementation methodologies, business process engineering, and ERP deployment projects. Strong knowledge of Oracle R12 modules including Inventory, BOM, WIP, Purchasing, and Order Management. Ability to create functional and technical specifications for Finance module interfaces, with deep understanding of finance data flows and table structures. Minimum 5 years of experience in Oracle Finance module implementations. Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, organizational, and prioritization skills. Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and operate effectively in matrix organizations. Expertise in SQL and PL/SQL performance tuning. Exposure to project management methodologies. Experience integrating third-party applications with Oracle Finance modules is preferred. Manufacturing and Planning module experience is a plus. With a steadfast commitment to delivering exceptional service to our clients, Bluelight excels in its focus on quality and customer satisfaction. With a presence across the United States and Central/South America, Bluelight is in an exciting phase of expansion, continually seeking exceptional talent to join its dynamic and diverse community. We're looking for a Business Analyst to turn business problems into clear, buildable requirements. You'll sit between our clients, our product team, and our engineers: running discovery, mapping processes, writing user stories and acceptance criteria, and making sure what we ship actually solves the problem it was meant to solve. You'll work across a mix of client builds, client maintenance engagements, and Bluelight's internal products, and you'll play a key role when new projects are being scoped and estimated. Responsibilities Lead stakeholder interviews and workshops with clients and internal teams to understand goals, current workflows, and pain points. Document current-state and future-state processes, business rules, data definitions, and edge cases. Support new-project sizing by breaking scope into epics and stories that engineering can estimate with confidence. Identify assumptions, risks, dependencies, and open questions early, and drive them to resolution. Write clear user stories with testable acceptance criteria in Jira. Partner with the Product Manager to prioritize and groom the backlog ahead of each two-week sprint. Work with UI/UX design in Figma to make sure flows and screens match the requirements, and flag gaps before development starts. Answer engineering questions during the sprint and keep requirements current as decisions are made. Work with QA to make sure acceptance criteria translate into solid test coverage. Support sprint demos and coordinate user acceptance testing with clients. Keep requirements documentation organized in Google Drive so decisions and their rationale are easy to find later. Make sure compliance, security, and audit requirements (including SOC 2 considerations) are captured as explicit requirements, not afterthoughts. Act as a trusted point of contact for clients on scope and requirements questions. Translate between business and technical audiences clearly and without jargon in either direction. Surface scope changes early and help the team and client understand the tradeoffs. Requirements 3+ years as a Business Analyst, Product Analyst, or similar role on software projects. Strong experience writing user stories and acceptance criteria in an agile/Scrum environment. Proven ability to run discovery sessions and turn ambiguous input into structured requirements. Comfort with process mapping and data modeling at a business level (flows, entities, relationships, rules). Hands-on experience with Jira; familiarity with Figma and collaborative docs. Excellent written and spoken English; comfortable leading client meetings with U.S. stakeholders. Enough technical literacy to have productive conversations with engineers about APIs, integrations, databases, and system constraints. Nice to Have Experience in an agency, consultancy, or software services environment juggling multiple clients. Exposure to regulated or compliance-heavy domains (e.g., SOC 2, telecom/outbound compliance, education, fintech). Experience writing requirements for integrations with third-party platforms. Familiarity with web application stacks (e.g., Laravel, React) and AWS. Experience supporting estimation or proposal work for new projects. Client Accounting & Advisory Services Location: Argentina Work Arrangement: Remote Employment Type: Full-Time, Independent Contractor Compensation: Up to USD 4,000/month Work Schedule: Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm EST About Convoy Finance We like working with people who move fast, think for themselves, and care about doing great work. Our clients are ambitious businesses, and we work directly with the founders and finance teams building them. That means we're not just looking at numbers all day. We get to see what's happening inside growing companies and help the people running them make better decisions. One week you might be leading a month-end close, and the next you could be helping a client work through a reporting issue, improve their financial processes or solve something completely new. You'll oversee accounting work across a portfolio of growing companies and work directly with international clients, founders, CFOs and senior finance professionals . You'll be responsible for making sure the accounting is accurate, the work gets done well and client deliverables stay on track. But we also expect you to look beyond the numbers: understand what's happening in the business, identify issues before they become problems and bring ideas to the table. This is a hands-on management role. You'll still be close to the accounting, while also reviewing work, guiding team members, managing priorities and helping clients navigate more complex accounting and finance questions. Our clients move quickly, and so do we. There will be deadlines, competing priorities and new problems to solve. We're looking for someone who is comfortable operating with a high degree of independence and can make good decisions without needing everything mapped out for them. As an Accounting Manager, you'll have significant ownership over your client relationships and the opportunity to grow into broader advisory, financial management and leadership responsibilities . What You'll Do You'll take ownership of: Managing a portfolio of client accounts, ensuring accurate and timely delivery of accounting and reporting work Leading and overseeing full-cycle accounting and month-end close, including reconciliations, journal entries, AP/AR and financial statement preparation Reviewing accounting work and ensuring quality, accuracy and consistency across client deliverables Preparing and reviewing financial statements, management reports and financial analysis Working directly with founders, CFOs and senior finance teams to answer questions, resolve issues and provide accounting guidance Managing client deadlines, priorities and deliverables, and proactively communicating when something needs attention Supporting year-end compilations, audits, reviews and tax-related work Identifying opportunities to improve accounting processes, systems and controls Coaching and supporting more junior members of the accounting team Taking ownership of more complex accounting issues and helping the team determine the right approach Supporting advisory and finance projects as they come up Building strong, long-term relationships with clients and becoming a trusted point of contact for their accounting needs Requirements What We're Looking For You have a Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field and 5+ years of relevant accounting experience , with significant experience in a client-facing accounting, public accounting, audit or advisory environment. Big Four experience is required for this role. We're looking for someone who has been exposed to high standards of quality, complex accounting work and demanding client environments, and who is ready to take that experience into a more hands-on, ownership-driven role. You're confident owning full-cycle accounting, month-end close and financial reporting , while also reviewing work, managing priorities and ensuring that client deliverables are accurate and delivered on time. You're comfortable working directly with clients, founders, CFOs and senior finance professionals . You communicate clearly in English and can explain what the numbers mean — not just what the numbers are. This role is 100% in English , both internally and with clients. If you want a role where you can keep learning, take real ownership and grow beyond traditional accounting , we'd like to hear from you. Client Accounting & Advisory Services Location: Argentina Work Arrangement: Remote Employment Type: Full-Time, Independent Contractor Compensation: USD 2,300-3,000/month Work Schedule: Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm EST About Convoy Finance We like working with people who move fast, think for themselves, and care about doing great work. That's pretty much how we run Convoy. We're a small finance and accounting firm working with technology, SaaS, fintech and Web3 companies across Canada and internationally. Our clients are ambitious businesses, and we work directly with the founders and finance teams building them. That means we're not just looking at numbers all day. We get to see what's happening inside growing companies and help the people running them make better decisions. One week you might be deep in a month-end close, and the next you could be helping a client solve a reporting issue, clean up their books or work through something completely new. We're a small team, too. Most of us are based in Toronto, with a few people working remotely around the world. There's very little bureaucracy, decisions happen quickly, and good ideas can actually turn into action. The Opportunity We're looking for a Senior Accountant who wants to be close to the action. You'll own accounting work across a portfolio of growing companies and work directly with international clients, founders, CFOs and senior finance professionals . You'll be responsible for getting the accounting right, but that's only part of it. We want you to understand the business behind the numbers, notice when something doesn't add up and be confident enough to ask questions. The clients we work with move quickly, and so do we. There will be deadlines, new problems to solve and plenty of opportunities to learn. You'll have the support of an experienced team, but you'll also be trusted to take ownership rather than wait for instructions. As you grow into the role, you'll have the opportunity to take on more complex accounting, finance and advisory work. What You'll Do You'll take ownership of: Full-cycle accounting and bookkeeping, including reconciliations, journal entries, AP/AR and month-end close Preparing and reviewing financial statements and management reporting Supporting year-end compilations, audits, reviews and tax-related work Working directly with clients to resolve accounting questions and issues Keeping client deliverables moving and communicating when something needs attention Finding ways to improve processes, systems and the way we work Supporting financial analysis and other client projects as they come up Requirements What We're Looking For You have a Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field and 4+ years of relevant accounting experience . You're comfortable owning full-cycle accounting, month-end close and financial reporting, and managing multiple clients and deadlines at the same time. You're confident communicating in English with clients and senior finance people . You can explain what the numbers mean, not just what the numbers are. This role would be a 100% in English. And you're someone who likes to figure things out . If something looks wrong, you investigate it. If you don't know the answer, you find it. If there's a better way to do something, you speak up. Experience with QuickBooks Online, Xero, Taxprep or CaseWare is a plus, as is experience in public accounting, audit, tax, SaaS, technology, fintech or Web3. CPA designation or active CPA pursuit is also a plus. Big Four experience is a must for this role. Benefits Why Convoy? You'll work with interesting companies, smart people and problems that don't always come with an instruction manual. You'll have direct exposure to founders and senior finance leaders and get to see how growing companies actually operate. Because we're small, your work is visible and your ideas can have an impact. We're remote-friendly, with team members working from Toronto and different parts of the world. We also make time for team lunches, happy hours and, when the numbers are good, the occasional team trip. It's fast-paced. It's challenging. And it's definitely not boring. If you want a role where you can keep learning, take real ownership and grow beyond traditional accounting , we'd like to hear from you. Compensation USD 2,300-3,000 per month , depending on experience and qualifications. This is a full-time independent contractor position . ¡Sumate a Primary y sé parte de la transformación digital del mercado financiero! En Primary buscamos un perfil técnico para incorporarse al área de Operaciones / SDP , con foco en la observabilidad, performance y confiabilidad operativa de plataformas de mercado . El rol tendrá una mirada preventiva sobre el comportamiento de los eventos críticos del mercado, interpretando métricas técnicas en contexto de negocio y colaborando en la evolución de un modelo de prácticas de confiabilidad y observabilidad dentro de la organización. Será una pieza clave para anticipar riesgos operativos y fortalecer la estabilidad de plataformas de misión crítica. Principales Desafíos y Tareas Generales del rol Monitoreo y Análisis Operativo Supervisar en tiempo real el comportamiento de plataformas críticas, analizando indicadores como volumen de órdenes, latencia, throughput, colas de procesamiento y tiempos de respuesta. Interpretar métricas de infraestructura (CPU, memoria, disco y red) en relación directa con la carga operativa y el flujo de mercado. Ejecutar el análisis exhaustivo de registros (logs) y telemetría en plataformas de observabilidad (como Datadog) para la identificación y diagnóstico preciso de anomalías, asegurando la detección temprana de incidentes que afecten la continuidad del servicio. Monitorear proactivamente la infraestructura y aplicaciones utilizando herramientas de APM, analizando fuentes de datos críticas para minimizar el tiempo medio de detección (MTTD) y proporcionar información clave para la remediación de fallas. Observabilidad y Confiabilidad Trabajar activamente con plataformas de observabilidad para analizar dashboards, interpretar alertas y detectar patrones anómalos o desvíos respecto al comportamiento esperado. Colaborar en la mejora continua de indicadores operativos, definición de umbrales y construcción de vistas que traduzcan métricas técnicas en impacto de negocio. Anticipación y Gestión Preventiva Identificar señales tempranas de picos de carga, degradación de performance o riesgo de saturación de capacidad. Elevar alertas preventivas y proponer acciones antes de que se materialicen incidentes, especialmente en jornadas de alta sensibilidad operativa. Contexto de Mercado Comprender la dinámica del mercado financiero y sus eventos relevantes (aperturas, cierres, vencimientos, jornadas de alta volatilidad), correlacionando dichos eventos con el comportamiento técnico de las plataformas. Sistemas y Performance Conocimientos sólidos de entornos Linux, fundamentos de performance de aplicaciones y administración de recursos. Comprensión de arquitecturas distribuidas, procesamiento de eventos y comportamiento bajo carga. Networking y Fundamentos Técnicos Conocimientos de latencia, throughput, conectividad y posibles cuellos de botella en entornos de red. Interés por la confiabilidad, estabilidad y prevención de incidentes. Competencias blandas valoradas Capacidad de análisis sistémico y pensamiento orientado a anticipación. You will analyze large-scale network telemetry, develop and evaluate methods for identifying malicious behavior, and improve the accuracy and efficacy of ExtraHop’s threat detection capabilities. Design, develop, and refine machine learning and AI-based methods that support ExtraHop’s products. Develop evaluation methods appropriate for cybersecurity data, including highly imbalanced datasets, incomplete labels, rare events, and changing attacker and network behavior. Conduct exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, model development, and error analysis using complex, high-volume datasets. Research emerging machine learning and AI techniques, relevant cybersecurity developments, and assess their applicability to ExtraHop’s products. Establish metrics and monitoring strategies for measuring model and detector performance over time. Communicate findings, limitations, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to technical stakeholders and product leaders. Provide technical leadership and mentorship to other data scientists through code reviews, design discussions, technical strategy, and contributions to the team’s analytical and engineering standards. Strong foundation in statistics, experimental design, machine learning, and model evaluation. Experience working with incomplete, noisy, or highly imbalanced data; performing detailed error analysis; and identifying the causes of false positives and false negatives. Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, experience with common data science and machine learning libraries, and the ability to write maintainable, tested, and reviewable code. Experience collaborating with software engineers to integrate data science methods into production systems. Strong problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and a track record of independently owning complex technical work. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical findings, uncertainty, and tradeoffs to varied audiences. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, or another quantitative discipline. Experience applying data science or machine learning to cybersecurity, fraud detection, abuse detection, anomaly detection, or another adversarial domain. Familiarity with Network Detection and Response, network protocols, threat detection, or incident investigation. Experience with time-series analysis, anomaly detection, actuarial modeling, clustering, graph analytics, or unsupervised and semi-supervised learning. Experience evaluating models in domains where positive examples are rare, labels are incomplete, and the underlying behavior changes over time. Experience with generative AI, large language models, agentic systems, or other emerging AI techniques. Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP. Overview We are hiring a Senior Staff Business Data Analyst to build the reporting, analytical, and AI layer on top of the sales data foundation — the views, semantic models, and dashboards the sales organization actually makes decisions with, and the data architecture that makes those views trustworthy. This is a senior individual contributor role. You are expected to operate at organizational scope: choosing what gets built, designing the models other analysts build on, setting the standard for how sales reporting works, and raising the capability of the analysts around you. The work runs from schema design through to the number a sales leader reads on a Monday morning, and you'll own the whole span rather than a slice of it. Responsibilities What you'll own: Reporting and dashboard architecture. Design and build the dashboards and reporting views the sales organization runs on — pipeline, coverage, win rate, forecast attainment, partner performance — as a coherent, maintainable set rather than an accumulating pile of one-off requests. You'll decide what becomes a governed asset, what stays ad hoc, and what should be retired. Semantic and consumption models. Build the layer between certified base tables and the people consuming them: reusable views, defined grains, conformed dimensions, and metric logic implemented consistently so that two dashboards asking the same question can't disagree. Data architecture contribution. Work alongside Data Operations on the underlying model — account, opportunity, contact, activity, contact role, campaign membership, account team, lead. You'll be one of the voices deciding how these fit together, and a primary source of the requirements that shape them, because you'll be the one whose reporting breaks if the grain or the keys are wrong. Identity and taxonomy in practice. Sales data arrives keyed differently in every system. You'll work daily in the resolution of account, company, firm, and customer identifiers, and in the product line / product family taxonomy — and you'll be the one who catches it when a metric resolves differently depending on which side of a join you're standing on. Metric definition and integrity. Contribute to and defend canonical KPI definitions: the base query, the grain, the exclusions, the edge cases. Where a number is contested, you'll be the person who can reconstruct exactly how it was calculated and why. Analysis that changes decisions. Beyond reporting, do the analytical work behind coverage models, buying-group completeness, funnel diagnostics, and territory and channel performance — for both direct and partner-led motions. Technical leadership. Set patterns, review other analysts' models, mentor, and write down the standards. Much of your impact will come through work you didn't personally build. Qualifications What you'll bring: Required 4+ years in business intelligence, analytics engineering, or data analysis, including experience as the senior technical voice on ambiguous, cross-team problems. Expert SQL. You can develop complex queries and structures that resolve high volume datasets and schemas across lines of business. Strong analytical data modeling: dimensional design, grain discipline, conformed dimensions, slowly changing dimensions, and the judgment to know when to denormalize. Deep hands-on experience with a modern BI platform (Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or equivalent) — including semantic layer design, extract and performance tuning, and governance of published assets. Direct experience with CRM data, Salesforce strongly preferred. You know the standard objects, their quirks, and what silently breaks when you join them without care. Experience building reporting that others depend on operationally, including the unglamorous parts: freshness expectations, breakage handling, change communication, and deprecation. Ability to work directly with sales leaders — translating a vague question into a defensible metric, and pushing back when the metric they asked for won't answer the question they have. Preferred Experience supporting sales, revenue, or partner/channel operations. Experience with partner or channel-led models, and reporting on partner relationships as first-class entities rather than as an afterthought on a direct-sales schema. Cloud warehouse or datalake depth (Databricks, Snowflake, or equivalent), transformation frameworks, orchestration, and version-controlled analytics code. Python or equivalent for analysis beyond what SQL handles well. Experience reporting through a major system migration, keeping numbers continuous while the underlying sources move. Familiarity with conversation-intelligence and sales-engagement data, and the data-quality realities of seller-created records. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet reporting deadlines. descripcion: Description Join Amazon Logistics as a Supply Chain Manager and help plan the capacity that keeps millions of packages moving to customers across North America. You'll take demand forecasts and turn them into capacity plans that make sure we have the right resources in the right places at the right time. In this role, you'll work with planning teams across Retail to solve real supply chain challenges. Your forecasts and capacity adjustments will directly impact our ability to deliver on our customer promise. You'll own demand forecasting for a rapidly growing logistics network, working across multiple teams to optimize how our network performs. Using advanced forecasting tools and systems, you'll make data-driven decisions at scale and shape the future of last-mile delivery through smart planning and continuous improvement. The impact you'll make is significant. You'll turn demand signals into capacity plans that balance efficiency with customer experience, mitigate capacity constraints before they impact delivery performance, and partner with technical teams to improve forecasting accuracy and planning systems. Your work will influence decisions that affect Amazon's logistics operations across North America. If you're passionate about supply chain optimization, thrive in fast-paced environments, and want to see the direct impact of your work on millions of customers, this is your opportunity to make a difference at scale. Key job responsibilities You'll develop and maintain accurate demand forecasts for your assigned region by analyzing historical data, market trends, and business inputs from cross-functional partners. You'll translate these forecasts into detailed capacity plans that ensure our delivery network has the right resources to meet customer demand while optimizing efficiency. You'll collaborate closely with retail planning teams and technology teams to gather inputs, validate assumptions, and align on capacity requirements. This includes regularly reviewing forecast accuracy, identifying gaps between planned and actual performance, and making real-time adjustments when business conditions change. A critical part of your role involves monitoring system configurations and making necessary adjustments to ensure forecasts flow correctly through planning systems. You'll troubleshoot discrepancies, resolve data quality issues, and partner with technical teams to improve forecasting tools and processes. You'll communicate forecast insights and capacity recommendations to leadership through regular business reviews, explaining variances and providing data-driven recommendations for network optimization. Throughout all of this, you'll drive continuous improvement in how we forecast demand and plan capacity across the logistics network. A day in the life Your week centers on publishing a 13-week demand plan that keeps Amazon's last-mile delivery network running. You start by analyzing demand signals, interrogating trends, and evaluating forecast accuracy using ML forecasting models. Mid-week, you collaborate with technology and data science teams to enhance forecasting models and align field partners on plan changes. As publication approaches, you finalize your forecast, communicate risks to leadership, and coordinate high-volume event planning. When curveballs hit—demand spikes, system issues—you diagnose root causes with data and drive solutions fast. Your expertise in data analysis and forecasting science plays a vital role in delivering for customers every day. About The Team You'll join a diverse team of problem solvers who thrive on collaboration and collective success. Our mission is to deliver accurate capacity plans that keep millions of packages moving to customers across North America. You'll work closely with teammates and cross-functional partners in retail planning, technology, and field operations to solve real-time capacity constraints and optimize network performance. If you're motivated to make an impact in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment where individual ownership drives collective results, you'll fit right in. Position Summary: Kraus is seeking a Supply Chain Planning Lead to establish, mature, and own the company’s supply chain planning capability as the business continues to scale. This role will create a single, data-driven demand signal across Sales, Product, Finance, Supply Chain, and Operations, improving forecast accountability, inventory planning, and cross-functional decision-making. The right individual will lead key processes and collaborate with stakeholders at Kraus and Delta to optimize working capital, customer service and operational costs The ideal candidate is a builder and player-coach: strategic enough to design the process, governance, and executive rhythm, but hands-on enough to manage forecasting, analytics, assumptions, and planning outputs. This role is intended for a manager who can influence across the organization, challenge assumptions constructively, and help move Kraus from reactive forecasting to a more disciplined, scalable planning model. Key Responsibilities Demand Planning Strategy & Ownership Collaborate with Delta and Masco Sister Companies to integrate Best Practices into Kraus processes. Develop the planning calendar, governance routines, forecast assumptions, and decision-making cadence. Build scalable data-driven processes that improve planning discipline and improve Forecast accuracy. Translate commercial strategy, customer trends, product launches, promotions, and market signals into an actionable demand outlook. Forecasting, Analytics & Performance Management Create and maintain short-, medium-, and long-term demand forecasts using historical trends, customer insights, seasonality, promotional activity, and business inputs. Establish and monitor KPIs such as forecast accuracy, forecast bias, forecast value-add, service-level impact, and inventory health. Identify demand risks, upside opportunities, and forecast variances; recommend practical actions to improve outcomes. Develop dashboards, reporting, and executive-ready insights that support data-driven planning decisions. S&OP / Consensus Planning Leadership Lead the monthly demand review and support the broader S&OP process. Facilitate consensus planning across Sales, Product, Finance, and Operations. Challenge and reconcile inputs from multiple functions to create one aligned demand plan. Present demand outlooks, key assumptions, risks, opportunities, and recommended decisions to leadership. Inventory, Supply & Business Partnership Partner with Supply Planning, Procurement, and Operations to balance demand, inventory, service levels, lead times, and working capital goals. Help identify stock-out exposure, excess/obsolete inventory risk, and demand-supply disconnects before they become operational issues. Support scenario planning related to growth initiatives, major customers, product transitions, promotions, and supply constraints. Develop and implement safety stock policies that are scalable and optimize Kraus’s inventory. Capability Building & Player-Coach Leadership Serve as the internal subject matter expert for demand planning best practices. Build tools, templates, routines, and planning discipline that can scale with the business. Coach cross-functional partners and any future planning team members on process, metrics, and expectations. Remain hands-on in the work while creating the foundation for a more mature planning function over time. Ideal Candidate Profile 8–12+ years of experience in demand planning, supply chain planning, forecasting, S&OP, inventory planning, or related disciplines. Experience building, improving, or transforming planning processes in a growth-oriented or evolving business environment. Strong analytical capability with the ability to turn complex data into clear business insights and practical recommendations. Comfortable influencing senior stakeholders across Sales, Finance, Product, Operations, and Supply Chain. Able to operate at both strategic and tactical levels: developing the roadmap while also executing the forecast and planning routines. Experience with ERP and planning systems such as SAP, Kinaxis, IBP, Oracle, Blue Yonder, or similar tools preferred. Position Summary The Senior Supply Chain Planner will play a critical role in advancing Banner’s inventory planning capability and stocking program strategy. This role will support and drive the processes, analytics, and cross-functional decision-making needed to improve in-stock levels at Banner and across distributor channels while balancing customer service, working capital, operational constraints, and product lifecycle priorities. The position will partner closely with Operations, Commercial, Product Management, Supply Chain, and regional teams to translate demand signals, stocking policies, service-level expectations, and product-family strategies into actionable inventory plans. The role will help define which products should be stocked, where inventory should be positioned, how stocking levels should be maintained, and how exceptions should be surfaced for decision-making. This position reports to Demand Planning Manager. This role requires working onsite at our Brooklyn Park, MN office five days a week. What You’ll Be Doing This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working Collaboratively and Individually, staying on top of tasks, and making a meaningful impact across teams and projects. Below are some key responsibilities of the role. Key Responsibilities Support the development and execution of Banner’s stocking program strategy, including P/S/N stocking recommendations, min/max logic, demand segmentation, and service-level targets. Analyze inventory availability, forecast inputs, demand behavior, backlog, open sales orders, lead times, and distributor requirements to identify gaps in in-stock performance. Partner with Product Management and Commercial teams to align stocking decisions with product-family strategy, lifecycle stage, customer promise, distributor expectations, and revenue priorities. Work with Operations and Supply Chain teams to translate stocking strategy into executable replenishment, production, and material plans. Develop reporting and dashboards to monitor in-stock levels, inventory health, service levels, forecast quality, slow-moving inventory, excess exposure, and stocking-policy effectiveness. Identify root causes of stockouts, inventory imbalances, past-due backlog, slow-moving inventory, and unmanaged stocking drift; recommend corrective actions and process improvements. Support monthly forecast and inventory reviews, product-family health reviews, and cross-functional stocking governance forums. Evaluate demand patterns using segmentation methods such as ABC/XYZ, runners/repeaters/strangers, lifecycle stage, customer concentration, and revenue contribution. Recommend stocking policy updates, safety stock assumptions, replenishment parameters, and exception-handling rules based on data, business priorities, and operational feasibility. Coordinate with distributor-facing and regional teams to understand channel inventory needs, availability gaps, lead-time expectations, and communication requirements. Help build standard work, planning tools, and repeatable processes that improve inventory decision quality and reduce reliance on ad hoc analysis. Escalate material stocking risks, service-level tradeoffs, or inventory exposure issues with clear options, financial impact, and recommended next steps. Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain analytical findings, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to both technical and business audiences. Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, structure problems, drive follow-up, and influence decisions without direct authority. Preferred Qualifications Experience in industrial manufacturing, automation, electronics, or distribution-supported business models. Familiarity with make-to-stock, configure-to-order, build-to-order, and engineer-to-order fulfillment models. Experience supporting SIOP, product lifecycle management, stocking strategy, distributor inventory programs, or product-family business reviews. Advanced Excel, data visualization, SQL, Power BI, Qlik, or similar analytics skills. APICS/ASCM CPIM, CSCP, or related supply chain certification preferred. Improved accuracy and discipline of stocking parameters, including P/S/N status, min/max levels, and replenishment assumptions. Clearer linkage between product-family strategy, commercial demand signals, and executable supply plans. Reduction in unmanaged inventory drift, excess exposure, and recurring planning exceptions. Repeatable reporting cadence and governance process for inventory and stocking decisions. descripcion: At Schaefer Plastics, we manufacture industry-leading solutions and drive responsible practices towards a sustainable future for generations to come. As a family-owned company since 1937, we are deeply committed to delivering exceptional customer care through high-quality, innovative waste and packaging solutions. Our customers and their satisfaction are paramount to our business; we strive to understand their needs and exceed their expectations at every turn. We are a global injection molding manufacturer, producing durable waste and recycling carts, and pioneering reusable packaging systems that reduce carbon footprints. Our dynamic and inclusive culture fosters personal and professional growth, making us an ideal employer for career advancement. Position Overview The Purchasing and Inventory Manager ensures the availability of materials needed to support production while improving profitability, inventory performance, and supplier reliability. This position oversees purchasing and inventory planning for raw materials, components, and packaging. The successful candidate will identify cost-saving opportunities, improve inventory turns, reduce working capital tied up in inventory, and support the company’s financial and operational goals. Key ResponsibilitiesPurchasing and Supplier Management Lead the procurement of plastic resins, recycled materials, components, packaging, and other materials required for production. Negotiate pricing, contracts, payment terms, lead times, and supply agreements to improve margins and cash flow. Monitor supplier performance related to cost, quality, delivery, and responsiveness. Build and maintain strong supplier relationships while identifying opportunities for alternative sourcing and improved terms. Research market conditions, pricing trends, supply risks, and other economic developments that may affect material availability or cost. Identify and implement cost-reduction and sourcing improvement initiatives. Address supplier performance concerns and coordinate corrective actions when necessary. Inventory Management and Planning Optimize inventory levels, safety stock, reorder points, and purchasing quantities to improve inventory turns while maintaining appropriate service levels. Monitor material requirements, inventory balances, production schedules, forecasts, and open purchase orders. Reduce excess, obsolete, and slow-moving inventory. Identify inventory discrepancies, determine root causes, and coordinate corrective action. Maintain accurate purchasing and inventory information within the company’s ERP/MRP system. Review purchasing and inventory reports to identify shortages, excess inventory, cost variances, and improvement opportunities. Support inventory audits, cycle counts, and reconciliation activities as needed. Operational and Financial Support Partner with Operations, Materials, Quality, Finance, Sales, Logistics, and other departments to ensure material availability and prevent production disruptions. Improve planning, forecasting, and supplier collaboration to reduce working capital requirements. Track procurement and inventory performance against established goals and key performance indicators. Provide regular updates regarding material availability, supplier performance, cost-saving initiatives, and inventory risks. Support budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis related to purchasing and inventory. Perform general clerical and administrative responsibilities, including data entry, maintaining purchasing and supplier records, preparing routine reports, processing documentation, and organizing procurement files. Perform other duties and support special projects as assigned. QualificationsRequired Five or more years of purchasing, inventory management, procurement, or supply chain experience within a manufacturing environment. Demonstrated experience managing suppliers, negotiating terms, and identifying cost-saving opportunities. Experience with inventory planning, demand forecasting, safety stock, and reorder-point management. Working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems and purchasing processes. Strong analytical, organizational, negotiation, and problem-solving skills. Ability to evaluate data, identify trends, and make sound business decisions. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. High level of accuracy and attention to detail. Preferred Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, Finance, or a related field. Experience purchasing plastic resins, recycled materials, packaging, or other materials used in plastics manufacturing. Experience supporting multiple manufacturing locations or business units. Professional certification in purchasing, supply chain, or inventory management. Success in This Role Success will be measured through improvements in: Inventory turns Working capital reduction Material cost savings Supplier on-time delivery Material availability Excess and obsolete inventory reduction Purchasing and inventory accuracy EBITDA improvement generated through procurement initiatives Why Join Schaefer Plastics? As a global leader in injection-molded plastic products, we manufacture waste and recycling carts, reusable packaging solutions, and other products that serve customers across a wide range of industries. Position Title: Director of Supply Chain Management Location: Reno, NV Reports To: VP Operations Department: Supply Chain Classification: Exempt Salary: $150,000 - $200,000 Position Summary The Director of Supply Chain is responsible for developing and executing strategies that support ASSA ABLOY Fenestration's growth, profitability, customer service, and operational objectives across its manufacturing, distribution, and sourcing operations. Leading the areas of demand planning, inventory management, purchasing, strategic sourcing, supplier performance, and Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP), this position serves as a key business partner to Operations, Sales, Engineering, Product Management, Finance, and Distribution. Success in the role requires balancing customer demand, inventory investment, supplier capacity, and operational requirements to ensure reliable product availability while optimizing working capital and overall supply chain performance. The position drives continuous improvement in forecasting accuracy, inventory optimization, material availability, supplier performance, and cost competitiveness through the development of scalable processes, performance metrics, and data-driven decision making. In addition, this leader is responsible for supply chain risk management initiatives, including supplier diversification, near-shoring strategies, tariff mitigation, trade compliance considerations, and sourcing optimization efforts that protect margins and strengthen business continuity. As a member of the senior management team, the Director of Supply Chain plays a critical role in supporting operational transformation, ERP maturity, and future growth by building a resilient, high-performing supply chain capable of supporting a complex, multi-site manufacturing and distribution network across North America. Key Responsibilities Supply Chain Strategy & Leadership Develop and execute supply chain strategies that support business growth, profitability, and operational excellence. Lead continuous improvement initiatives across purchasing, planning, inventory management, and supplier performance. Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for service, inventory, supplier performance, cost savings, and working capital. Build organizational capability through coaching, mentoring, and development of supply chain team members. Global Sourcing, Tariff Management & Supply Chain Risk Develop and execute sourcing strategies that reduce supply chain risk while supporting cost, quality, and service objectives. Lead tariff mitigation initiatives, including supplier relocation, product translation, near-shoring, country-of-origin optimization, and trade compliance strategies. Monitor global trade policies, tariffs, duties, freight markets, geopolitical risks, and economic trends that may impact supply continuity or profitability. Partner with Finance, Operations, and Commercial teams to quantify tariff exposure and implement action plans that protect margins and customer competitiveness. Evaluate and develop sourcing opportunities across North America and global supply markets to reduce dependence on single-source suppliers and high-risk regions. Lead strategic supplier transitions, localization initiatives, and capacity expansion efforts to support business growth and changing market conditions. Develop contingency plans for critical commodities, key suppliers, and supply chain disruptions. Identify opportunities to optimize distribution networks, transportation strategies, and inventory positioning to improve customer service while minimizing total landed cost. S&OP and Demand Planning Lead and facilitate the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Partner with Sales, Product Management, Finance, and Operations to develop accurate demand forecasts. Align demand, inventory, supplier capacity, and business objectives through a structured planning process. Drive forecast accuracy improvements and inventory visibility throughout the organization. Inventory Management & Supply Planning Establish inventory strategies and policies that balance customer service requirements with working capital objectives. Develop safety stock methodologies and inventory planning processes across manufacturing and distribution locations. Monitor inventory levels, turns, obsolescence, and service performance. Drive optimization of inventory deployment across facilities and distribution centers. Purchasing & Strategic Sourcing Lead all sourcing and procurement activities, including supplier selection, negotiations, contracting, and performance management. titulo: Mgr III, Supply Chain, Enterprise S&OP
descripcion: Description Amazon's technology supply chain supports a complex and rapidly evolving portfolio of infrastructure, end-user equipment, and technology products across thousands of locations globally. As the business scales, we are building mechanisms that do more than consolidate information and react to problems after they emerge. We are looking to build the ability to identify risk early, evaluate scenarios, make clear trade-offs, and translate decisions into coordinated action across the organization. We are seeking a senior leader to build and lead the enterprise S&OP capability within Supply Chain Planning. This leader will manage a team responsible for establishing a common S&OP and risk-management mechanism across the business. The team will connect the plan with the multiple execution layers of the organization, ensuring material risks are identified early, scenarios are evaluated, trade-offs are understood, decisions are made at the appropriate level, and actions are driven to closure. This role will also help define the digital evolution of S&OP. The successful candidate will partner with Product, Data, Analytics, and Technology teams to move S&OP from a largely human-orchestrated process toward an increasingly automated, exception-based, and intelligence-driven decision system. This includes integrating signals across systems, automating risk identification, enabling scenario modeling, and applying advanced analytics and AI to improve the speed, quality, and scalability of supply chain decisions. The ideal candidate combines strong supply chain planning fundamentals, business judgment, analytical capability, technology orientation, and cross-functional leadership. They must be comfortable operating in ambiguity, challenging assumptions, simplifying complex problems, and influencing senior leaders across Supply Chain, Technology, Finance, Procurement, Operations, and customer organizations. This is not a traditional reporting or meeting-management role. The successful candidate will build S&OP into a forward-looking enterprise decision mechanism that improves decision quality, business predictability, prioritization, and customer outcomes. Key job responsibilities Lead and develop a team responsible for Enterprise S&OP/IBP, risk management, scenario planning, and cross-functional orchestration Establish and continuously improve the S&OP operating model connecting Plan with the multiple execution layers of the organization. Create a single, forward-looking view of material demand, supply, inventory, capacity, supplier, and customer risks, translating signals into prioritized decision points. Lead scenario analysis and evaluate trade-offs across customer service, inventory, cost, capacity, and business priorities. Establish escalation and decision mechanisms that enable leaders to focus on material risks and exceptions rather than status reporting. Ensure S&OP decisions translate into clear ownership, actions, timelines, and measurable closure across cross-functional teams. Define performance mechanisms that measure risk aging, decision effectiveness, mitigation progress, and customer delivery predictability. Partner with Product, Data, Analytics, and Technology teams to define the digital roadmap for S&OP, including signal integration, risk intelligence, scenario modeling, automation, and decision-support capabilities. Identify where fragmented systems, data defects, or manual processes require humans to act as integration layers and drive scalable solutions to eliminate these dependencies. Advance the use of analytics and AI to automate risk identification, prioritize exceptions, identify root causes, and support scenario-based decision making. Build closed-loop mechanisms where execution constraints, decisions, and actual outcomes continuously improve future planning and risk management. Simplify redundant processes and governance mechanisms while developing scalable capabilities that support new businesses, products, geographies, and fulfillment models. A day in the life In this role, you may begin the day reviewing emerging demand, supply, inventory, and execution signals with your team and determining which risks require intervention. You may work with Demand and Supply Planning leaders to evaluate a constrained product, challenge assumptions behind a customer requirement, or quantify the service and inventory implications of alternative decisions. Your team will then ensure those decisions are translated into actions across the appropriate execution layers and tracked through closure. You may also spend time with Product or Technology teams defining how a manual planning activity can be automated, determining which signals should feed a risk model, or designing how scenario-planning capabilities should support future business decisions. The role requires balancing today's operating needs with the longer-term goal of building a more scalable system where humans spend less time assembling information and more time making high-quality decisions.
